deals.fate: The starting gun of the era. Acquired by AOL in 1999.
Survivor. Fell ~95% in 2000–01, then compounded into one of the best stocks ever. Holding through was the trade — and almost nobody did.
Survivor — real unit economics from day one.
Fell ~99% in the crash — then survived and became Booking Holdings. A 99% loss that was still, eventually, a win.
~$8B valued at debut; bankrupt Jul 2001 after burning >$800M. The idea (grocery delivery) was right — 20 years early.
All-time record first-day pop. Down >90% within a year.
Liquidated Nov 2000 — 268 days from IPO to shutdown.
Briefly worth more than its parent 3Com's entire stake implied — an arithmetic impossibility the market shrugged at. Top-ticked the bubble almost to the day.

lessons: The first-day pop is a cost, not a gift: retail buys at the close, which is historically the single worst systematic entry.
Survivorship is brutal and unpredictable in real time: Amazon and Pets.com looked like the same bet in 1999. Both fell >90% or died; only one came back.
Narrative eras produce clustered IPOs, and clustered IPOs produce clustered wreckage — the 2000-01 vintage underperformed for years.
The window closes fast: 476 IPOs in 1999, ~80 in 2001. Companies that waited for a better price got no price.
Even the era's TRUE story (the internet changes everything) didn't save buyers who paid any price for it. Being right about the technology is not the same trade as being right about the stock.

spacex_outlook.position: ≈$140 (Aug 17) vs $135 offer; ~$1.85T market cap; 12-mo sell-side avg target ~$227 (treat sell-side targets on a 2-month-old mega-IPO with heavy skepticism — most raters were underwriters).

scenarios.name: Bull
scenarios.text: Starlink subscriber growth compounds, Starship reaches operational cadence, index inclusion (already in Nasdaq-100) forces passive buying, and the scarcity premium of THE space asset holds. Sell-side path: $200+.

scenarios.name: Base
scenarios.text: Base rates apply: median mega-IPO chops around its offer price for quarters. At ~$1.85T the market already prices decades of execution; revenue (~mid-tens of $B) implies a multiple where good news is expected, not rewarding. Lockup expiry ~Dec 2026 adds supply. Range-bound $110–170.

scenarios.name: Bear
scenarios.text: Any Starship setback, Starlink competition (Kuiper), key-person/political volatility around Musk, or a broader AI/space sentiment unwind. The July slide below offer showed how little floor there is. $100 or below revisits the post-IPO low.
